claim: Blending (finding a shared abstraction between two unrelated inputs, then a coherent merged concept) is harder for LLMs than association or analogy. Across 35 LLMs, valid outputs were 59.0% association, 53.4% analogy, 43.4% blend; humans (N=75) 22.1%, 32.9%, 12.8%.
agent_test: Same random entity pairs, equal tokens: plain blend prompt vs prompt with an explicit generic-space step; score valid-blend rate with a fixed judge panel.

claim: The LLM failure in blending is finding the generic space, not describing the blend: a valid generic space was found only 43.4% of attempts, but given a valid one a coherent blend followed 97.1% of the time.
agent_test: Split the blend operator into generic-space proposal plus verifier, then describe. Compare to one-shot at equal tokens; check where failures fall.

claim: Different LLMs invent the same properties for a blend (inventive homogeneity): 19.9% (412/2,070) of invented concepts repeat at least 2 properties of another model's; blends reuse 94.7% vs analogy 36.3% (at least 1 property); same-provider reuse 9.3% vs 4.1% across providers. Several samples from one model give less diversity than they seem to. Gap search 2026-11-01: the same sameness shows inside one model (Beyond the Hivemind: baseline pairwise similarity above 0.8 for all five models, 0.810 to 0.880, on open prompts, not blends). Sampling alone did not fix it (persona plus extreme temperature together got below 0.7). Showing the model its earlier answers gave the most distinct new paths on CREATE but used extra calls, so an exclusion list at equal tokens is still untested.
schema_part: G (diversity, anti-fixation), memory of used blends
agent_test: Generate N blends per item with and without an already-used-properties exclusion list; count distinct property sets at equal tokens.

claim: Scaffolds that improved LLM blending outputs add a named middle step plus a check: explanation/shared-attribute step (IEI, Midjourney mean rank 2.40 to 1.98; win rate vs experts 0.26 to 0.35); generic-space-invariant transfer with diagnostic retry (mean MI 2.75 plain, 3.69 strong one-shot prompt, 4.56 full loop; N=100 raters); bridge-then-expand (ideas per pair 0.87 to 2.03). A strong one-shot prompt closes much of the gap. Gains of added steps are small or model-dependent: spreading activation on GPT-4o gave +1.4 to +3.4 points over CoT (+3.0 to +5.0 over base) on emergent property induction, while an oracle best-of-5 gave +17 over base; a structure-score refinement loop (PRISM) won human forced choice 57.65%, with smaller gains with a stronger model.
agent_test: Ablate one-shot vs staged vs staged+diagnostic at equal total tokens on a text blending task.
audit_note: Song et al. (CCPT, GPT-4o, emergent property induction): Base 40.8, CoT 42.4, SA(LLM) 43.8, SA(ConceptNet) 45.8, SA(both) 45.2, oracle best-of-5 57.8, so spreading activation is +1.4 to +3.4 over CoT (+3.0 to +5.0 over base); the stated +2.4 to +5.0 over CoT matches neither. Other figures (IEI 2.40 to 1.98 and 0.26 to 0.35; MI 2.75/3.69/4.56 with N=100; PopBlends 0.87 to 2.03; PRISM 57.65%) check out.
claim_before_audit: Scaffolds that improved LLM blending outputs add a named middle step plus a check: explanation/shared-attribute step (IEI, Midjourney mean rank 2.40 to 1.98; win rate vs experts 0.26 to 0.35, length-controlled); generic-space-invariant transfer with diagnostic retry (mean MI 2.75 plain, 3.69 strong one-shot prompt, 4.56 full loop; N=100 raters); bridge-then-expand (ideas per pair 0.87 to 2.03, N=10). A strong one-shot prompt closes much of the gap. Gap search caveat: gains of added steps are small or model-dependent. Spreading activation over CoT on GPT-4o was +2.4 to +5.0 points on emergent properties (Song 2025), while best-of-5 by an oracle gave +17; a structure-score refinement loop (PRISM) won human forced choice 57.65% but smaller with a stronger model.

claim: Typicality-based blending (Lieto and Pozzato TCL) combines a head and a modifier by building probability-ranked scenarios of kept properties; the most probable scenario is often trivial or inconsistent (20.4% trivial scenario discarded), so a human or rule must pick the creative one. Reasoning stays EXPTIME-complete.
agent_test: Implement head+modifier property inheritance with defeasible conflict handling in code; compare to LLM free-text combination on pet-fish style items, scoring consistency and non-triviality.

claim: Shrager's view application (1987, N=7 BigTrak learners) models theory change as copying a stored view, merging the current theory into it, and keeping only coherent theories. This shrinks search (about 5,760 theories after 2 view applications vs about 124 million at the unconstrained simple level) but can give coherent-but-wrong theories (BASIC view on a digital watch). The system tracked a human for up to 6 view applications (12 interactions of about 52).
agent_test: Library of 8 to 20 stored mental-model views; compare view-seeded hypothesis generation to blank-slate on hidden-device tasks at equal tokens; measure steps to correct theory and rate of coherent-wrong theories.

claim: A coded blender (analogy mapping plus evolutionary search over part relations, Cunha et al. 2017) reproduced 23 of 39 (59%) human-drawn visual blends and made novel ones; blends judged good let raters name both inputs more often (pig-angel 70% vs 10%). Evidence is small (9 drawers, 30 raters, 3 concept pairs, 5 raters per blend) and the good/bad split was set by the authors.
schema_part: O (coded blend operator: map then search with fitness)
agent_test: Use a fitness of relations preserved from each input to rank LLM-proposed blends; test whether the ranking agrees with a blind panel.

claim: GPT-3 bridge and attribute generation is only partly reliable: connecting concepts valid 56.0 to 58.7% each (93.3% of pairs have at least one good among five); entity attributes 57% accurate (adjectives 79%, catchphrases 35%); rater agreement 0.41 (Pearson). Best-of-k plus a verifier is needed.
schema_part: G (verify), O (blend: propose k then filter)
agent_test: Propose 5 bridges, filter with a checker; compare to 1 draw at equal tokens with a current model (numbers are GPT-3, 2021-era).

claim: Language models retrieve concept associations far better than a knowledge base: on a simile set, precision at 1000 candidates was 5.90 (ConceptNet) vs up to 66.38 (best language-model row). Row labels in the table are ambiguous in text extraction.
agent_test: Sanity check only: let the LLM, not a fixed graph, propose cross-domain links.

claim: Raising sampling temperature gives new combinations but not ones no artist would think of; reaching those needed explicit search for low cognitive-availability combinations (perplexity proxy). Judged by GPT-4 and embedding distance only, no humans.
agent_test: Compare high-temperature sampling vs an explicit avoid-the-most-common-pairings rule at equal tokens, judged by a blind panel.

claim: Interactive blend tools with one LLM call per operation give mixed results: Misty mean satisfaction 3.2/5 (SD 1.3) over 103 operations; 44 above neutral (43%), 28 neutral, 31 below; only 5 of 14 agreed it expressed their intent.
agent_test: None directly; a reminder that single-call blends need an intent check (G) before use.

claim: No independent replication of any computational blending result was found among the opened sources. Evaluations are worked examples (TCL, topological-group blend, Deep Dream) or small user studies (N = 9, 10, 14, 30, 75, 100). Gap search: forward-citation lists (Semantic Scholar) for Xu 2026 (6 citers), KOMBINE (8), CCPT (2) and Eppe 2018 (87 titles) show no direct re-run; Eppe 2018 and Divago chapters stay unopened (403/404).
agent_test: Treat every blend result as a hypothesis; run our own ablation before adding any operator.
audit_note: Minor: Semantic Scholar citer counts (6, 8, 2) and Cunha's 'no evidence of an implementation' were verified; the negative claim is only about the opened sources, and user-study sizes N=9, 14, 75 were not individually re-checked.

claim: Prompt-level effects read as blending (Sato, speculative) and diffusion embedding mixing (Matsuhira: true blend peaks at ratio 0.5, BCD 0.621 vs MCD 0.862; averaged 0.389 vs 0.471) are image or speculative results with no text-reasoning test. Mixed depictions are more common than truly fused ones.
agent_test: None; do not use these to justify a text blend operator.
audit_note: Minor: Matsuhira's BCD 0.621 / MCD 0.862 at ratio 0.5 and 0.389 / 0.471 averaged over ratios match Table; MCD counts any depiction of both concepts so 'mixed more common than fused' is by definition; Sato's paper is speculative and reports no counts.

claim: LLM judges are a weak link in blend evaluation: the Schapiro 3-judge panel agrees with humans 75% even when unanimous; GPT-4 judges novelty in the alien-combination study; in the visual-metaphor pipeline one model is both generator and judge; a GPT-4.1 rubric scores the adapter paper. Gap search adds measured human-judge agreement: GPT-4o judge vs human relevance Pearson 0.85 (Song, 300 pairs, narrow property rating); Gemini 2.5 Pro vs humans on creativity r=0.708 over 27 method cells but only 0.342 over 267 items, novelty 0.224 ns (UoT); CREATE specificity judge r=0.67 with 2 authors (alpha 0.68), factuality judge precision 0.52 on incorrect relations. Agreement is good only for narrow, decomposed checks.
agent_test: Score our blend tests with a different model family than the generator, plus a small human spot check.
audit_note: Minor: UoT novelty 0.224 is at method level (n=27); Schapiro's 75% is on the 96 unanimous judgments (66% panel-majority overall); the Cho et al. 'GPT-4.1 rubric' detail was not located in the text read; 'good only for narrow checks' is the author's synthesis.

claim: Concept steps outrun rendering in images: GPT-4o combination descriptions integrated objects and theme in 36 of 40 DALL-E 3 cases, yet 10 of 36 well-formed descriptions still failed to render. In text, the generic-space step is the bottleneck (K02).
agent_test: None beyond K02.

claim: Song et al. 2025 (peeled apple) measure noun-phrase conceptual combination with property types (emergent, canceled, component), not blending. Scaffolds: Base, CoT, spreading activation (retrieve and filter related concepts, up to 5 rounds), and a best-of-5 oracle. GPT-4o emergent property E: 40.8 base, 42.4 CoT, 45.8 SA(ConceptNet), 57.8 oracle; noun phrase completion 20.4, 23.1, 26.9, oracle 38.9 (human 38.0). Models lean on parent properties; GPT-4o names the property type right only 56.4% (humans 81%).
schema_part: O (blend operator step 2: consistency of kept properties)
agent_test: On our blend items, ask for each kept property whether it still holds in the merged concept; compare with CoT at equal tokens and with best-of-5 plus a verifier.

claim: No study tests a blend operator (generic space plus verifier) on a downstream reasoning benchmark against a strong one-shot prompt at equal tokens. The nearest is Universe of Thoughts C-UoT (analogue, mechanism, solution): on HypoArena (Qwen3-14B) average win rate 19.5 vs CoT 18.8 and exploratory search 32.7; on three creative tasks (GPT-4o) it was best on one by LLM judge (Society 0.649) and tied on human rating. Full C-UoT beat its no-transfer ablation in 58.3% of comparisons (50 = chance).
agent_test: Use CresOWLve creative subset (factual subset as control) to run plain vs generic-space-plus-verifier at equal tokens; accept the operator only if it beats one-shot on accuracy, not on blend ratings.

claim: Coherent-but-wrong blends are real but their rate is unmeasured. KOMBINE shows subtly wrong generic spaces that apply to one input only (yeast and bread vs photosynthesis); Song 2025 shows models keep parent properties the combination cancels. No study counts how often a consistency check catches them.
agent_test: Check the generic space and each kept property against each input separately; seed the test with known coherent-wrong cases and count catches.

claim: Judge agreement with humans is good only for narrow decomposed checks and weak for whole-item creativity: Song judge r=0.85 on property relevance (300 pairs); CREATE specificity r=0.67 (75 paths), creative utility r=0.55 vs two authors (105 queries); UoT Gemini vs human creativity r=0.708 at method level (n=27) but 0.342 per item (n=267), novelty 0.224 not significant. No separate-family judge was tested for blend validity.
agent_test: Judge blend validity with a different family than the generator on property-level questions; spot check by hand; compare methods only over many items.
audit_note: Minor: CREATE creative-utility r=0.55 is the average of 0.51 and 0.48 against two annotators; UoT novelty 0.224 is method level (n=27); 'no separate-family judge tested' is an absence claim that cannot be verified from the sources.

claim: Parallel files already hold a better-tested neighbour of the blend operator: a staged analogy-then-solve step raised novelty at equal call counts for three frontier models (A09.04-K25, A11.02-K29), with grounding and one-to-one mapping checks from the candidate-inference files. Breadth, not validity, is what those tests measure. Blend-specific machinery should wait for a head-to-head.
agent_test: Run analogy-then-solve with grounding check against the generic-space blend operator on the same items.

claim: Text-only LLM blending studies from 2025 to 2026 beyond KOMBINE: Song 2025 (combination, 12,315 items), CREATE 2026 (associative paths, judge-validated), Universe of Thoughts (combinational operator), DRAT (association tests do not predict ideation, rho +0.57 for the one that mixes remote association and divergence). None tests a generic-space step, a verifier and a downstream reasoning score together.
agent_test: Treat the generic-space-plus-verifier as unproven; plan our own ablation.

claim: The Xu 2026 staged-pipeline gain (4.56 vs 3.69 for one strong prompt) has no independent reproduction. A different group (PRISM) tests a verifier-in-loop refinement for visual metaphors and finds gains over zero-shot (57.65% human preference), smaller with a stronger model, and a structure score that is a worse chooser than zero-shot (82.5% vs 88.5%). Not a replication.
agent_test: Cap the retry loop; measure gain per model strength.

claim: Single-source within-model homogeneity: five small instruct models show baseline similarity 0.810 to 0.880 between samples of one prompt. An already-used-properties exclusion list for blends has not been tested at equal tokens; iterate-with-previous-answers on CREATE raised distinctness at extra calls.
agent_test: Compare N blends per item with and without an exclusion list at equal tokens; count distinct property sets.
